- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to over-forecast (especially after spikes), so reduce forecast by 5–15% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >40% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias of 10–20% for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 40), model tends to hold or over-forecast — adjust downward by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days — adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the window (first 5–7 days) — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent 7-day average to avoid overconfidence.
